risks: _md_blocks | medium | The 'table' block extraction uses a separator detection that may incorrectly skip valid rows if they consist entirely of characters in set '-: ' (e.g., a row with a single dash). This could drop table rows. | Add test case with a row like '| - |' to verify behavior.

handoff.purpose: Implements markdown block parsing (_md_blocks), HTML rendering (_render_md), and the analyse_once entry point for tree analysis.

symbols.name: _md_blocks
symbols.note: Parses lines of text into blocks: paragraphs, headings (h3, h4), quotes, tables, unordered lists. Returns list of (kind, payload) tuples.

symbols.name: _render_md
symbols.note: Converts block list from _md_blocks into HTML string. Uses _inline for inline formatting (not shown in chunk).

symbols.name: analyse_once
symbols.note: Performs a single walk of the repository tree, returning (reach report, switch report). Uses reach_mod.analyse and switches_mod.analyse. Optionally uses cached_index with refresh=True.

observations.what: The _md_blocks function uses a nested function flush_para to accumulate paragraph text before adding a new block.

Table parsing in _md_blocks checks if all cells consist only of characters in set '-: ' to skip separator rows; this may be too broad (e.g., a cell with a single dash would be considered a separator).

In table parsing, the condition `if not all(set(c) <= set("-: ") and c for c in cells):` uses `set(c)` on each cell; for a cell like '---', set(c) is {'-'}, which is subset of {'-',':',' '}, so it would be excluded. This is intentional for separator rows, but might exclude valid rows with cells like ' - ' (space dash space) which set(c) would be {' ', '-'} also subset.

The _render_md function renders quotes as `

` instead of `

`, which may be a design choice but semantically unusual.
analyse_once catches Exception when importing cached_index, which could mask import errors or other issues.
analyse_once returns a tuple of two values from reach_mod.analyse and switches_mod.analyse; the order is (reach, switch).
